_about: Used by qa_map.py ONLY to flag stakeholder groups that this kind of organisation usually has but the evidence has not surfaced. It never adds a group. A warning means 'ask about this in the next interview', not 'it exists'. Keywords are matched (case-insensitive) against group name, business unit, org units and summary.

expected_groups.label: Regulator (e.g. CAAS)
expected_groups.why: Approves maintenance organisation changes; can gate go-live of any system that holds airworthiness records.
expected_groups.probe: Which regulator approvals does this change touch, and who talks to them informally?

expected_groups.label: Licensed engineers / certifying staff
expected_groups.why: Personal legal sign-off gives them veto power that does not show on the org chart.
expected_groups.probe: Who do the certifying staff actually take advice from before they trust a new record system?

expected_groups.label: Quality and safety
expected_groups.why: Owns audit trail and procedure change control.
expected_groups.probe: Who can stop a process change on safety grounds, and how often do they?

expected_groups.label: Shift supervisors / line leads
expected_groups.why: Handover networks carry the real work; they are the channel for frontline sentiment.
expected_groups.probe: How does information move between shifts, and who is trusted to relay it?

expected_groups.label: Union or staff association
expected_groups.why: Formal consultation duties on role or shift changes.
expected_groups.probe: Which changes trigger consultation, and who engages the union informally?

informal_channels: technical authority that outranks line management
regulator relationships held by one or two individuals

expected_groups.label: Project / programme management
expected_groups.why: Controls schedule and resourcing that every other group competes for.
expected_groups.probe: Who decides when a workstream is allowed to pause for training?

expected_groups.label: Technical authority / design engineers
expected_groups.why: Informal authority over how work is done.
expected_groups.probe: Whose judgement is final when the process and the engineering view disagree?

expected_groups.label: Safety, health and environment
expected_groups.why: Stop-work authority.
expected_groups.probe: Where has safety shaped how systems or procedures were introduced before?

expected_groups.label: Site / field operations
expected_groups.why: Where adoption actually happens, often on poor connectivity and in shifts.
expected_groups.probe: Who on site do others copy when a new tool arrives?

expected_groups.label: Subcontractors / suppliers
expected_groups.why: Outside the reporting line but inside the process.
expected_groups.probe: Which subcontractors must change how they transact, and who manages them day to day?

informal_channels: relationships between project and site that bypass the PMO

expected_groups.label: Political / ministerial oversight
expected_groups.why: Sets mandate and tolerates or rejects visible risk.
expected_groups.probe: What does the parent ministry need to see, and who carries that message?

expected_groups.label: Finance and procurement
expected_groups.why: Gates spend and vendor engagement under public rules.
expected_groups.probe: Which approvals have historically slowed change, and who clears them informally?

expected_groups.label: HR / organisation development
expected_groups.why: Owns role, grade and scheme changes.
expected_groups.probe: Which role changes need HR or union alignment before they can be announced?

expected_groups.label: Middle management / division heads
expected_groups.why: Translate mandate into local priority; frequent point of quiet resistance.
expected_groups.probe: Which division heads are most likely to delay quietly?

expected_groups.label: Frontline officers
expected_groups.why: Absorb the change and inform citizen-facing quality.
expected_groups.probe: How do frontline officers hear about change today, and whom do they trust?

informal_channels: long-serving officers acting as unofficial helpdesks
cross-agency working groups that decide before committees do

expected_groups.label: Regulator
expected_groups.why: Licence conditions constrain operations and data.
expected_groups.probe: Which licence obligations does the system change touch?

expected_groups.label: Control room / operations
expected_groups.why: Cannot tolerate disruption; its sign-off is practical veto.
expected_groups.probe: What cutover windows does operations accept, and who negotiates them?

expected_groups.label: Asset management / maintenance
expected_groups.why: Primary users of plant maintenance and asset data.
expected_groups.probe: Who owns the asset master data and is anyone resisting cleansing it?

expected_groups.label: Shared services / finance
expected_groups.why: Process owners for finance and supply chain transactions.
expected_groups.probe: Which shared-service teams carry the most manual workarounds?

expected_groups.label: Shareholder / parent entity
expected_groups.why: Mandate and reporting expectations.
expected_groups.probe: Which board members follow this programme closely?

informal_channels: union and management relationships dating back decades
control-room veterans consulted on operational risk

expected_groups.label: Risk and compliance
expected_groups.why: Can block change on control grounds.
expected_groups.probe: Which controls does this change alter, and who signs off?

expected_groups.label: Technology / operations
expected_groups.why: Delivery capacity and change freeze calendars.
expected_groups.probe: Who owns the release calendar and its exceptions?

expected_groups.label: Front office / relationship managers
expected_groups.why: Revenue owners with strong informal power.
expected_groups.probe: Whose workload objections get escalated successfully?

expected_groups.label: Regulator
expected_groups.why: Notification and outsourcing rules.
expected_groups.probe: Which notifications does the change need?

expected_groups.label: Internal audit
expected_groups.why: Independent challenge on controls.
expected_groups.probe: Has internal audit already commented on this programme?

informal_channels: senior bankers with direct line to the CEO
operations managers who unofficially fix front-office issues
compliance officers consulted informally before formal submissions

expected_groups.label: Clinicians (doctors)
expected_groups.why: High autonomy; adoption depends on peer opinion more than mandate.
expected_groups.probe: Which clinical leaders do others follow on new systems?

expected_groups.label: Nursing
expected_groups.why: Largest user group, with their own leadership line.
expected_groups.probe: Who among nurse managers shapes how a change lands on the ward?

expected_groups.label: Allied health and pharmacy
expected_groups.why: Process hand-offs that rarely appear in the sponsor's view.
expected_groups.probe: What workarounds exist between pharmacy, wards and billing?

expected_groups.label: Patient safety and quality
expected_groups.why: Stop-the-line authority.
expected_groups.probe: How does patient safety review system changes?

expected_groups.label: Administration and finance
expected_groups.why: Owns the transactional process the system changes.
expected_groups.probe: Where does administration depend on clinicians' goodwill?

informal_channels: department heads who set peer norms
clinician champions who bypass the IT queue
